rows.note: Use 節目 as the all-purpose noun for a television or radio program.

example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 go3 zit3 muk6 gei2 hou2 siu3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday construction for showing someone an object, result, or piece of information.
Use 騷 for a live entertainment show or performance rather than a broadcast program.

example.english: Tonight's show has a live band.
example.traditional: 今晚嗰場騷有現場樂隊。
example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 go2 coeng4 sou1 jau5 jin6 coeng4 ngok6 deoi6

rows.note: Use this when showing something to be true or vindicating yourself to someone who doubted you.

example.english: I’ll show you that I wasn’t lying.
example.traditional: 我會證明畀你睇我冇講大話。
example.jyutping: ngo5 wui5 zing3 ming4 bei2 nei5 tai2 ngo5 mou5 gong2 daai6 waa6

rows.note: Use this spoken phrase when facts or evidence allow someone to tell or infer a conclusion.

example.english: The look on your face can show that you’re tired.
example.traditional: 睇你個樣就睇得出你攰喇。
example.jyutping: tai2 nei5 go3 joeng2 zau6 tai2 dak1 ceot1 nei5 gui6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for something becoming visible, appearing on a screen, or turning up at a place.

example.english: An error message can show up suddenly on the screen.
example.traditional: 個錯誤訊息突然喺畫面上出現咗。
example.jyutping: go3 co3 ng6 seon3 sik1 dat6 jin4 hai2 waa6 min6 soeng6 ceot1 jin6 zo2

rows.note: Use 展覽 for an organized exhibition of art, animals, or other items.

example.english: This show has lots of local artworks.
example.traditional: 呢個展覽有好多本地藝術品。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 zin2 laam5 jau5 hou2 do1 bun2 dei6 ngai6 seot6 ban2
